title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the study of the stratification 'at infinity' of the moduli multiplicities M_{g,ν}, i.e. the boundary of a Deligne–Mumford/Knudsen-type compactification. The surrounding pages work in local, smooth algebraic multiplicities (stacks).

Notation. D_{d_*}, for a strictly decreasing sequence d_* = {d_0 > d_1 > ... > d_r}, is a smooth multiplicity attached to a flag of degeneration strata. D^*_{d_*} is the corresponding open (exact) stratum. Θ_{d_0} is the normal-crossings boundary divisor on D_{d_0}.

The problem being served. The previous page reduces the study of 'specialization' homomorphisms between fundamental groups of open strata, π_1 P^*_{d_*} → π_1 P^*_{d'_*} for a subflag d'_* ⊂ d_*, to the hard case d'_0 < d_0. In that case there is a morphism (223) D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*}. This is a local morphism of smooth multiplicities of codimension d_0 − d'_0, and it does not respect the open strata.

This page:
1. The commutative square (224) has top row D_{d_0..d_r} → D_{d'_0..d'_r} and bottom row D_{d_0,d'_0} → D^*_{d'_0}. The vertical arrows are étale. The bottom arrow is a local immersion of codimension d = d_0 − d'_0.
2. In the case where d'_* is d_* with d_0 removed (d'_0 = d_1), the square is cartesian, and this is trivial.
3. A marginal NB treats the general case. It factors D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*} as a finite étale map onto a stratum, followed by a cartesian square over D_{d_0,d'_0} → D_{d'_0}.
4. It then considers the induced map (225) D^*_{d_*} → D_{d'_*}. Note the star on the source only: the image is not in the open stratum D^*_{d'_*}.
5. D_{d'_*} is equipped with the normal-crossings divisor Θ_{d'_*}, the pullback of Θ_{d_0}. Θ^{(p)}_{d'_*} denotes its 'p-skeleton', the locus where p local branches meet.

The next page concludes the argument:
- (225) is a local isomorphism of D_{d_*} onto Θ^{(d)}_{d'_*}, identified with D_{\tilde d'_*}, where \tilde d'_* = (d_0, d'_0, ..., d'_r).
- Hence D_{d_*} → D_{d'_*} factors as a finite étale map followed by the inclusion of the codimension-d multiple-intersection locus.

In modern terms: the closure of a codimension-d boundary stratum is, up to finite étale (normalization) maps, the d-fold self-intersection locus of the normal-crossings boundary divisor. The 'specialization' maps between strata are therefore normalization-of-NC-stratum maps. This is the standard local structure of the boundary of \bar M_{g,n}, organised via the gluing maps. It is used here to analyse the fundamental-group maps between strata (the 'tour de Teichmüller'/Lego picture).
errors: No real mathematical error is visible. The statement that the vertical arrows are étale presupposes working with local (henselian/étale-local) multiplicities, as the previous page indicates.
The equation labels are being renumbered on the fly: the square is labelled (223)/(224), and (225) appears twice. This is a bookkeeping slip, not a mathematical one.

ideas.what: Local structure of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,ν}: a closed stratum of codimension d maps finite-étale onto the d-fold self-intersection locus (d-skeleton) of the normal-crossings boundary divisor.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of \bar M_{g,n} by stable graphs; gluing/clutching maps as normalizations of boundary strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); in the stable-graph form, Arbarello–Cornalba and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the 'structure à l'infini' and the Teichmüller tower informally

ideas.what: Specialization maps between fundamental groups of open strata, π_1 P^*_{d_*} → π_1 P^*_{d'_*}, used to organise the tower at infinity.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoids at infinity / tangential base points; Teichmüller (Lego) tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Cartesian base-change square reducing the strata map to the case of a single divisor drop (d'_0 = d_1).
ideas.modern_name: Base change along boundary strata / normal-crossings local charts

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine local geometry of normal-crossings boundary strata, of the kind that is now standard in the theory of \bar M_{g,n}. It is interesting historically as part of Grothendieck's unpublished working-out of the 'structure à l'infini' behind the Esquisse, but it contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The diagram label is (224), apparently overwritten, not (223). The text later refers to 'les diagrammes (224)'.
The bottom-right entry of the square is D^*_{d'_0}, with an exclamation mark stressing the star.

The bracketed remark should read roughly: 'Dans le cas particulier (ce qu'on a vu) où d'_* = {d_1 > ... > d_r}, le diagramme (224) est cartésien — plus précisément [crossed: ...], il est cartésien si d'_0 = d_1, et c'est trivial.'
The parenthetical after (225) reads roughly: '(attention, on n'a pas mis une * en exposant à D_{d'_*}: D^*_{d_*} seulement, non : D_{d'_*} !)'.
Marginal NB: 'Dans le cas général, ...: D_{d_*} —fini étale→ D^T_{d'_*}? —cart→ D_{d'_*}, over D_{d_0,d'_0} → D_{d'_0}, with a dotted arrow D_{d_*} ⇢ D_{d_0}'.
